views.name: classroom_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT classroom.building AS building,
       classroom.room_number AS room_number,
       classroom.capacity AS capacity
FROM classroom
views.description: One row per classroom with its identifying location and capacity; basic cohort of all classrooms.
validated_on: Could you please gather a list of all the buildings, except 'Gates', along with the number of classrooms they contain? I really need to know the count of classrooms for each building!

Determine the number of classrooms categorized as 'Large', 'Medium', or 'Small' based on their capacities in the 'Lamberton' building, with only those classrooms having a capacity greater than 20 included in the count.
counter_examples: Buildings with classrooms having an average capacity between 50 and 100, what is their average department budget?
Unveil the portals within the edifices, those chambers that hold audiences ranging from a gathering of 50 souls to a populous 100. Which sanctuaries boast such voluminous capacity?

views.name: section_room_assignment
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  section.course_id,
  section.sec_id,
  section.semester,
  section.year,
  section.building,
  section.room_number,
  section.time_slot_id
FROM section
JOIN classroom ON section.building = classroom.building AND section.room_number = classroom.room_number
views.description: Sections mapped to classroom locations (building + room_number) plus their course and term identifiers. Useful to find which sections meet in which rooms.
validated_on: Could you please gather a list of all the buildings, except 'Gates', along with the number of classrooms they contain? I really need to know the count of classrooms for each building!
counter_examples: Unveil the portals within the edifices, those chambers that hold audiences ranging from a gathering of 50 souls to a populous 100. Which sanctuaries boast such voluminous capacity?

views.name: large_classrooms_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.building,
  c.room_number,
  MAX(c.capacity) AS capacity_max,
  COUNT(s.course_id) AS section_count
FROM
  classroom AS c
LEFT JOIN
  section_room_assignment AS s
  ON c.building = s.building AND c.room_number = s.room_number
GROUP BY
  c.building,
  c.room_number
views.description: Aggregate counts of sections per classroom and maximum capacity per classroom to support questions about room utilization and availability of large rooms.

views.name: building_classroom_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  classroom.building AS building,
  COUNT(classroom.room_number) AS classroom_count
FROM classroom
GROUP BY classroom.building
views.description: Pre-aggregated counts of classrooms per building. Keeps one row per building with the raw count measure; does not apply any question-specific building filters so it can be reused for different exclusions or selections.

views.name: department_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  department.dept_name AS dept_name,
  department.building AS building,
  department.budget AS budget
FROM department
views.description: One-row-per-department with canonical department attributes (name, building, budget) suitable for filtering, aggregation, and joins.

views.name: department_budget_stats
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name,
  d.building,
  d.budget,
  (SELECT AVG(budget) FROM department) AS avg_budget_all_departments
FROM department AS d
views.description: Per-department aggregated budget measures; exposes budget and allows comparison to overall/partitioned averages. Keeps one row per department for reuse in budget-related comparisons.

views.name: department_with_courses
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  d.building AS building,
  d.budget AS budget,
  c.course_id AS course_id,
  c.title AS title,
  c.credits AS credits
FROM department AS d
JOIN course AS c
  ON c.dept_name = d.dept_name
grain: course_id (one row per course assigned to a department)
views.description: Denormalized mapping of departments to their courses (one row per course) including department attributes and course attributes; useful for queries that need department-level filters combined with course-level details.

views.name: department_core_7
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  d.building AS building,
  d.budget AS budget,
  LENGTH(d.dept_name) AS dept_name_length
FROM department d
views.description: Canonical department-level rows exposing identifying and numeric budget info and building; normalizes types and exposes dept name length for downstream classification.
validated_on: What are the names and buildings of the first three departments when ordered alphabetically by department name?
Could you provide the average budget for each department?
counter_examples: Can you find the names and locations of those top-level departments with the most funding?

In the realm where academic pursuits intertwine with fiscal prowess, what is the count of unique realms (departments) that navigate budgets beyond $100,000 and offer courses that soar above the basic tier of 2 credits, categorized by budget strata of opulence, moderation, and frugality?

views.name: instructors_by_department
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  instructor.ID AS ID,
  instructor.name AS name,
  instructor.dept_name AS dept_name,
  instructor.salary AS salary
FROM instructor
views.description: One row per instructor with department affiliation and salary; useful for selecting top-paid instructors per department or aggregating instructor counts and salary stats.

views.name: top_instructor_per_department
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name,
  i.ID as "ID as top_instructor_ID",
  i.name as "name as top_instructor_name",
  i.salary as "salary as top_instructor_salary",
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY d.dept_name ORDER BY i.salary DESC) as salary_rank
FROM department d
JOIN instructors_by_department i ON i.dept_name = d.dept_name
views.description: Per-department top instructor(s) by salary using a salary rank; keeps ties if salaries equal. Exposes rank so callers can pick the top (rank = 1) or top-N.

views.name: building_capacity_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  building,
  COUNT(room_number) AS classroom_count,
  AVG(capacity) AS avg_capacity
FROM classroom
GROUP BY building
views.description: Per-building aggregated classroom measures: number of classrooms and average capacity. Keeps raw measures so callers can apply thresholds or further filters.

views.name: department_with_building_budget
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  dept_name,
  building,
  budget
FROM department
views.description: Departments with their building and budget. Exposes department row-level data for joining to building-level filters (e.g., include departments located in particular buildings).
validated_on: What are the names and buildings of the first three departments when ordered alphabetically by department name?
For buildings linked to the Civil Engineering department, what are their names and average classroom capacities, ordered from highest to lowest average capacity?
counter_examples: Could you please find out all the buildings that have exactly two different departments occupying them? I need to know specifically the names of those buildings!

views.name: department_classroom_capacity
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.building,
  c.room_number,
  c.capacity,
  d.dept_name,
  d.budget AS department_budget
FROM classroom AS c
JOIN department AS d
  ON c.building = d.building
views.description: Classrooms annotated with the department(s) housed in the same building and the department budget — useful to analyze room capacities by department location.

views.name: departments_by_building
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.building AS building,
  COUNT(d.dept_name) AS department_count
FROM
  department d
GROUP BY
  d.building
views.description: Aggregated counts of departments per building; useful for queries that group or filter buildings by how many departments they host. Preserves building as the grain and raw count as a measure.

views.name: departments_by_budget_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  department.dept_name AS dept_name,
  department.building AS building,
  department.budget AS budget,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY department.budget DESC) AS budget_rank
FROM department
grain: dept_name  -- one row per department with rank
views.description: Departments with a budget rank (dense_rank or rank) so callers can easily select top-N or ties at top. Exposes budget and computed rank ordered by budget descending.

views.name: departments_budget_stats
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  COUNT(dept_name) AS dept_count,
  MIN(budget) AS budget_min,
  MAX(budget) AS budget_max,
  AVG(budget) AS budget_avg,
  SUM(budget) AS budget_sum
FROM department
grain: singleton  -- one row containing global budget aggregates
views.description: Aggregate budget statistics across all departments (min, max, avg, sum, count). Useful for comparisons and threshold-based queries.

views.name: classrooms_by_building
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.building,
  c.room_number,
  c.capacity,
  bc.classroom_count AS rooms_in_building_count,
  ROUND(bc.avg_capacity, 2) AS avg_capacity_in_building
FROM classroom AS c
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    building,
    COUNT(*) AS classroom_count,
    AVG(capacity) AS avg_capacity
  FROM classroom
  GROUP BY building
) AS bc
  ON c.building = bc.building
grain: room_number, building  -- one row per classroom
views.description: Classroom-level rows with capacity and building, plus a precomputed aggregation per building (count of rooms and average capacity). Keep raw rows available; aggregations help typical group-by queries.

views.name: department_building_classrooms
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  d.building AS department_building,
  c.room_number AS room_number,
  c.capacity AS capacity
FROM department_core d
JOIN classroom_core c
  ON d.building = c.building
grain: dept_name, room_number  -- one row per (department, classroom-in-same-building) match
views.description: Denormalized relation joining departments to classrooms by building. Each row links a department to a classroom located in the same building. Useful to compute per-department building-level classroom statistics.

views.name: students_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  student.ID AS ID,
  student.name AS name,
  student.dept_name AS dept_name,
  student.tot_cred AS tot_cred
FROM student
views.description: One row per student with their identifying and departmental attributes. Useful as a base cohort for filtering by department, name, or other student-level queries.

views.name: department_details
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  department.dept_name AS dept_name,
  department.building AS building,
  department.budget AS budget
FROM department
views.description: One row per department with building and budget information. Useful for joining department attributes to people, courses, or aggregation by department.
validated_on: What is the total number of distinct courses offered by the Physics department?

views.name: student_with_department
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  student.ID AS ID,
  student.name AS name,
  student.dept_name AS dept_name,
  student.tot_cred AS tot_cred,
  department.building AS department_building,
  department.budget AS department_budget
FROM student
LEFT JOIN department ON student.dept_name = department.dept_name
views.description: Denormalized student rows augmented with their department's building and budget. Useful for queries that need student info together with department attributes without repeating join logic.

views.name: classroom_core_21
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  classroom.building AS building,
  classroom.room_number AS room_number,
  CAST(classroom.capacity AS numeric) AS capacity
FROM classroom
views.description: One row per classroom with canonicalized key and numeric capacity exposed. Keeps building, room_number and capacity for filtering, grouping and classification.

views.name: classroom_counts_by_band
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  band,
  COUNT(*) AS classroom_count
FROM (
  SELECT
    -- propagate canonical classroom identity so the view remains joinable if needed
    building,
    room_number,
    capacity,
    band
  FROM (
    -- base input placeholder: expects caller to supply band for each classroom.
    -- By default, expose all classrooms without assigning bands (NULL band)
    SELECT
      c.building AS building,
      c.room_number AS room_number,
      c.capacity AS capacity,
      NULL AS band
    FROM classroom_core c
  )
)
GROUP BY band
views.description: Generic aggregation skeleton that can count classrooms by an external banding label. Accepts rows with a derived 'band' label and returns counts per band. This view does not hard-code band definitions; expects band assignment to be done before or in question ops.

views.name: advisor_instructor_link
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  advisor.s_ID AS s_ID,
  advisor.i_ID AS i_ID
FROM advisor
views.description: One row per advisor assignment linking student to instructor (advisor). Exposes the advisor instructor id so queries can filter or join to instructor attributes.

views.name: instructor_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  instructor.ID AS ID,
  instructor.name AS name,
  instructor.dept_name AS dept_name,
  instructor.salary AS salary
FROM instructor
views.description: Canonicalized instructor records with key identity and primary attributes useful for filters and joins (department, salary, name). Keeps raw salary for numeric comparisons.

views.name: advisors_with_instructor_attributes
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  advisor.s_ID AS s_ID,
  advisor.i_ID AS i_ID,
  instructor.name AS instructor_name,
  instructor.dept_name AS instructor_dept,
  instructor.salary AS instructor_salary
FROM advisor
JOIN instructor ON advisor.i_ID = instructor.ID
views.description: Denormalized view of advisor assignments enriched with instructor attributes. One row per student-advisor pair including instructor salary and dept for easy filtering/aggregation by instructor properties.

views.name: students_with_advisor_and_credits
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  student.ID AS student_id,
  student.name AS student_name,
  advisor.i_ID AS advisor_i_id,
  student.tot_cred AS tot_cred
FROM student
LEFT JOIN advisor ON advisor.s_ID = student.ID
WHERE advisor.s_ID IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per student with their advisor id and academic credits; useful to filter students by advisor existence and credit thresholds.

views.name: instructors_with_salary_and_teaches
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  instructor.ID AS instructor_id,
  instructor.name AS instructor_name,
  instructor.salary AS salary,
  teaches.course_id AS teaches_course_id,
  teaches.sec_id AS teaches_sec_id,
  teaches.semester AS teaches_semester,
  teaches.year AS teaches_year
FROM instructor
LEFT JOIN teaches
  ON instructor.ID = teaches.ID
views.description: Instructor-level rows exposing salary and their teaching assignments (section keys and semester). Useful to find instructors meeting salary thresholds and whether they taught in particular semesters.

views.name: advisor_to_instructor_teaches_link
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  student.ID AS student_id,
  advisor.i_ID AS advisor_i_id,
  instructor.ID AS instructor_id,
  instructor.salary AS salary,
  teaches.course_id AS teaches_course_id,
  teaches.sec_id AS teaches_sec_id,
  teaches.semester AS teaches_semester,
  teaches.year AS teaches_year,
  student.tot_cred AS tot_cred
FROM student
JOIN advisor ON advisor.s_ID = student.ID
JOIN instructor ON instructor.ID = advisor.i_ID
LEFT JOIN teaches ON teaches.ID = instructor.ID
grain: student.ID, teaches.course_id, teaches.sec_id, teaches.semester, teaches.year (one row per student - advisor's teaching assignment)
views.description: Denormalized mapping from student -> advisor -> instructor -> instructor's teaching assignments. Exposes student id, advisor instructor id, instructor salary and teaching semester/year to enable combined filters across these relationships.

views.name: course_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  course.course_id AS course_id,
  course.title AS title,
  course.dept_name AS dept_name,
  course.credits AS credits
FROM course
views.description: One row per course with its department and credit value. Exposes course-level metadata needed to test existence of courses meeting credit thresholds.

views.name: department_with_course_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name,
  d.building,
  d.budget,
  COUNT(c.course_id) AS qualifying_course_count
FROM
  department d
LEFT JOIN
  course c
ON
  c.dept_name = d.dept_name
  AND c.credits >= 0
GROUP BY
  d.dept_name,
  d.building,
  d.budget

semantic_filters.credits: no question-specific threshold; view counts courses meeting a non-restrictive credit condition placeholder (credits >= 0) so callers can apply thresholds

views.description: Denormalized view at the department level that indicates whether the department offers any course satisfying a credit threshold and includes the department budget. Keeps one row per department with a simple boolean/count measure of qualifying courses.

views.name: courses_with_credits
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  course.course_id AS course_id,
  course.title AS title,
  course.dept_name AS dept_name,
  course.credits AS credits
FROM course
views.description: One row per course with its identifying info and credit value; used to filter cohorts of courses by credit and join to departments or sections.
validated_on: What is the total number of distinct courses offered by the Physics department?
counter_examples: Could you please list all the titles of courses that don't have any prerequisites? I also need to know their department names along with the total number of courses offered in each department. Make sure to organize the results by department name and then by course title!

views.name: department_dim
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  d.building AS building,
  d.budget AS budget
FROM department d
views.description: Department dimension with canonical department identifier, building and budget for filtering, grouping and joining.

views.name: dept_courses_denorm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.course_id AS course_id,
  c.title AS title,
  c.credits AS credits,
  c.dept_name AS dept_name,
  d.building AS department_building,
  d.budget AS department_budget
FROM course c
LEFT JOIN department d
  ON c.dept_name = d.dept_name
grain: course.course_id -- one row per course (with its department info)
views.description: Denormalized relation linking courses to their departments (one row per course with department attributes). Useful for counting departments meeting course-based criteria or grouping departments by course measures.
validated_on: What is the total number of distinct courses offered by the Physics department?

views.name: course_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  course.course_id AS course_id,
  course.title AS title,
  course.dept_name AS dept_name,
  course.credits AS credits
FROM course
views.description: One row per course with canonical course identifiers and basic attributes; exposes course id, title, department and credits for joins and filtering.
validated_on: Could you please find all the courses that have more than one prerequisite? I need to know the title, number of credits, and the department name for each of these courses, and make sure that the credits and department names are not missing!
counter_examples: Which courses in the curriculum have ventured into the realm of multiple prerequisites, requiring more than a solitary stepping stone of knowledge, and what are their names, credit values, and departments?

views.name: course_prereq_relationship
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  prereq.course_id AS course_id,
  prereq.prereq_id AS prereq_id
FROM
  prereq
views.description: Rows linking a course to each of its prerequisite course ids. Keeps one row per (course_id, prereq_id) pair to serve as the cohort for counting distinct prerequisites.
counter_examples: Which courses in the curriculum have ventured into the realm of multiple prerequisites, requiring more than a solitary stepping stone of knowledge, and what are their names, credit values, and departments?

views.name: course_prereq_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.course_id AS course_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.prereq_id) AS prerequisite_count
FROM prereq p
GROUP BY p.course_id
views.description: Aggregated counts of distinct prerequisites per course. Keeps course_id and the distinct prerequisite_count to enable filtering courses by how many prerequisites they have.

views.name: departments_count_per_building
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.building AS building,
  COUNT(DISTINCT d.dept_name) AS distinct_dept_count
FROM
  department AS d
GROUP BY
  d.building
views.description: Aggregated counts of distinct departments per building. Produces one row per building with the number of distinct departments located there.

views.name: building_department_listing
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.building AS building,
  GROUP_CONCAT(d.dept_name) AS dept_names
FROM department d
GROUP BY d.building
views.description: Lists departments grouped by building, with an array/concatenated list of dept_name values per building. Useful to inspect which departments occupy a building.

views.name: prereq_agg_by_course
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.course_id AS course_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.prereq_id) AS distinct_prereq_count,
  MIN(p.prereq_id) AS example_prereq_id
FROM prereq p
GROUP BY p.course_id
views.description: Aggregated prerequisities per course: counts of distinct prereq course ids and a representative list/measure. Useful to find courses with multiple prerequisites or to join counts to course rows.

views.name: course_with_prereq_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.course_id,
  c.title,
  c.credits,
  c.dept_name,
  COALESCE(pac.distinct_prereq_count, 0) AS distinct_prereq_count
FROM
  course AS c
LEFT JOIN
  (SELECT course_id, COUNT(DISTINCT prereq_id) AS distinct_prereq_count
   FROM prereq
   GROUP BY course_id) AS pac
ON c.course_id = pac.course_id
grain: course.course_id -- one row per course, with aggregated prereq info
views.description: Denormalized view joining courses to their aggregated prerequisite info. Exposes course attributes alongside prereq counts so callers can apply filters like 'more than one prereq' or exclude NULLs in course columns.

views.name: course_prereq_counts_41
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.course_id AS course_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.prereq_id) AS distinct_prereq_count
FROM
  prereq p
GROUP BY
  p.course_id
views.description: Aggregated counts of distinct prerequisites per course. Exposes the raw count measure so callers can filter for courses with multiple prerequisites or join counts back to course details.

views.name: department_budget_stats_42
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  dept_name,
  COUNT(*) AS rows_count,
  COUNT(budget) AS non_null_budget_count,
  SUM(budget) AS budget_sum,
  AVG(budget) AS budget_avg
FROM department
GROUP BY dept_name
views.description: Pre-aggregated budget measures per department: count of rows, count of non-null budgets, sum of budgets, and average budget computed in SQL. Keeps dept_name as the grouping key so downstream queries can apply additional filters/sorts or join other dimensions.

views.name: courses_without_prereq
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.course_id,
  c.title,
  c.dept_name,
  c.credits
FROM course AS c
LEFT JOIN prereq AS p
  ON c.course_id = p.course_id
WHERE p.course_id IS NULL
views.description: All courses that do not appear as a course_id in the prereq table (i.e., courses with no listed prerequisites). Exposes course identity and its department for joining and grouping.

views.name: sections_with_classroom
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.course_id,
  s.sec_id,
  s.semester,
  s.year,
  s.building,
  s.room_number,
  s.time_slot_id
FROM section_room_assignment AS s
views.description: Section rows augmented with the referenced classroom identifiers (building, room_number) so sections can be associated with classroom capacity and other classroom attributes.

views.name: classroom_capacity
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  classroom.building AS building,
  classroom.room_number AS room_number,
  CAST(classroom.capacity AS numeric) AS capacity
FROM classroom
views.description: Canonical classroom records with capacity numeric and identifying building+room_number; useful for joining to sections and computing aggregates by room or by building.

views.name: prereq_pairs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  prereq.course_id AS course_id,
  prereq.prereq_id AS prereq_id
FROM prereq
views.description: Row-level representation of prerequisite relationships between courses. Each row is one (course -> prerequisite) pair to support existence checks and graph queries.

views.name: dept_course_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  COUNT(c.course_id) AS dept_course_count
FROM
  department d
LEFT JOIN
  course c
ON
  d.dept_name = c.dept_name
GROUP BY
  d.dept_name
views.description: Count of courses per department. One row per department with the raw count of courses; useful for joining back to courses to report department-level course totals.

views.name: course_base_48
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  course.course_id AS course_id,
  course.title AS title,
  course.dept_name AS dept_name,
  course.credits AS credits
FROM course
views.description: Canonical projection of courses exposing primary identifiers and descriptive attributes for filtering, grouping, and joining.

views.name: prerequisite_links
views.body_sql:
SELECT course_id, prereq_id
FROM prereq
grain: one row per (course_id, prereq_id) prerequisite link
views.description: One row per prerequisite relationship linking a course to each of its prerequisites; useful to detect courses that have any prerequisites or to traverse prerequisite graph.

views.name: courses_without_prereqs_candidate
views.body_sql:
SELECT c.course_id,
       c.title,
       c.dept_name,
       c.credits
FROM course AS c
LEFT JOIN prereq AS p
  ON c.course_id = p.course_id
WHERE p.course_id IS NULL
grain: one row per course that has zero rows in prereq linking to it
views.description: Candidate cohort of courses that currently have no recorded prerequisites (derived by anti-joining courses to prerequisite links). Keeps course identifiers and titles for downstream selection.

views.name: teaches_session_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  teaches.ID AS ID,
  teaches.course_id AS course_id,
  teaches.sec_id AS sec_id,
  teaches.semester AS semester,
  teaches.year AS year
FROM teaches
grain: teaches.ID, teaches.course_id, teaches.sec_id, teaches.semester, teaches.year -- one row per teaches record
views.description: One row per teaching assignment (an instructor teaching a specific section in a semester/year). Exposes identifying columns for joins and common session-level filters (semester, year).

views.name: instructor_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  instructor.ID AS ID,
  instructor.name AS name,
  instructor.dept_name AS dept_name,
  instructor.salary AS salary
FROM instructor
views.description: Canonical instructor rows with key identifying columns and main attributes used for joining and filtering (keeps ID and name and dept and salary).

views.name: teaches_with_instructor
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  teaches.ID AS "teaches.ID",
  teaches.course_id AS "teaches.course_id",
  teaches.sec_id AS "teaches.sec_id",
  teaches.semester AS "teaches.semester",
  teaches.year AS "teaches.year",
  instructor.name AS "instructor.name",
  instructor.dept_name AS "instructor.dept_name",
  instructor.salary AS "instructor.salary"
FROM teaches
LEFT JOIN instructor ON teaches.ID = instructor.ID
grain: teaches.ID, teaches.course_id, teaches.sec_id, teaches.semester, teaches.year  -- one row per teaches record (with instructor info)
views.description: Denormalized teaching assignments joined to instructor basic info. Useful for counting distinct instructors per semester/year or filtering by instructor attributes.
